sections.heading: Primitive and built-in categories
sections.markdown:
- `i64` — default signed integer
- `f64` — default floating-point number
- `string` — UTF-8 string
- `bool` — `true` / `false`
- `()` — Unit, no return value
- exact structural objects `{ field: T }`
- `Array<T>`, `Map<K,V>`, `Set<T>`, `Channel<T>`, `JSON.Value`, `JSON.Object`, `Array<u8>`, `BigInt`

sections.heading: Explicit conditions
sections.markdown: Conditions accept only non-nullable `bool`. Use `value != null` for presence, or `flag == true` / `flag ?? false` for nullable booleans. Explicit comparisons preserve branch narrowing.

sections.heading: Nullable
sections.markdown: Each T? adds an independent outer Optional layer. i64?? distinguishes outer None, Some(None), and Some(Some(7)); layers never flatten. Implicit widening wraps an exact element once, so typed i64 cannot directly fill i64??. JSON.Value? is a legal independent outer Optional even though JSON.Value itself includes JSON null. Some/None describe tags, not newly introduced source constructors. These are language contracts; complete Source admission and execution qualification are tracked separately in Task 319.

sections.heading: Collections
sections.markdown: The new-XIR implementation subset is Array<T> as described in spec §17.26, including nested admitted arrays and function elements through the unified constructed-type pool. Elements must be copyable and storable; unit, internal cells, views and unadmitted noncopyable resources reject. Inventory presence does not qualify other container or user struct/class families.

sections.heading: Tuple types
sections.markdown: Tuples preserve ordered field types and independently owned immutable values. Flat destructuring uses exact arity and evaluates its RHS once; module bindings publish as one prepared group (spec §17.35). Unit fields carry no payload and do not admit ordinary Unit generic arguments or formals. Nested tuple values do not imply admitted nested patterns; Sendable remains the conjunction of fields and wrapping grants no execution permission.

sections.heading: Admitted XIR floating semantics
sections.markdown:
In the new-XIR subset, f32 and f64 preserve their original IEEE precision across arithmetic and output (spec section 17.27). Zero signs and gradual subnormal values are preserved; invalid floating operations produce canonical NaN, and finite nonzero division by zero produces signed infinity. VM and native AOT use the same integer-only arithmetic implementation with independent exact-result tests; this does not imply the entire language or standard library is migrated.

Frozen next Atomic cutover: runtime f64 admits every binary64 payload and preserves bits in transport; runtime f32 and CONST_FLOAT retain canonical-NaN restrictions. Arithmetic, conversions including same-width conversion, and negation canonicalize NaN results. This expanded carrier domain remains pending implementation and qualification (spec 2.3.2/17.24/17.27).

sections.heading: Logical Unit parameters
sections.markdown: Unit is the empty Tuple and retains one logical argument even with zero frame payload. Fixed Unit READ formals in free functions, callable/closures, methods/constructors, interface signatures and generic definitions use canonical zero Values and the common checked argument plan. Calls retain arity and effects; other Unit statements do not become SSA values. Generic Unit-argument domains and full fault/safety qualifications remain separate obligations. See compilation pipeline section17.68.

sections.heading: Anonymous record identities
sections.markdown: Anonymous record identity uses the exact field set and field types. Canonical field order uses unsigned UTF-8 bytes; expression evaluation still follows source order exactly once. Only identifier field names and dot access are allowed; quoted keys and string indexing belong to Map/JSON. Shapes do not implicitly convert to named structs or acquire user interfaces. Structural constraints accept anonymous records only, expose exact read-only fields at definition time, and cannot use extra actual fields to repair an invalid generic body. The compiler currently has an owned, bounded canonical-field preparation helper with an explicit source-to-field permutation. This helper does not yet admit anonymous records through Source, Checked, VM/native, structural witnesses or full resource/safety qualification.
